audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is described as a blanket 'dodge' you must wait out. Riot's text is narrower than that, and the narrower reading is playable.
audit.why: Riot's Counter Strike: Jax 'dodges all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattacks, stunning all surrounding enemies' — 17/15/13/11/9. It dodges ATTACKS. Comet Spear and Shield Vault are abilities, so their damage still lands through the window; what you lose is your autos, and what you must not do is be mid-channel when the counterattack stuns. That turns 'never fight into E' into 'keep casting, stop auto-attacking, and do not be channelling'.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike dodges attacks, not abilities — keep casting Q and W through it, drop the autos, and never be mid-Aegis-Assault when it stuns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Relentless Assault is never mentioned, and Grandmaster-at-Arms is described only as 'huge resist stacking'.
audit.why: Riot's passive: 'Jax's consecutive basic attacks continuously increase his Attack Speed' — so the longer any trade runs, the faster he gets, which is the mechanical reason short trades beat long ones here. Riot's ultimate also has a passive half: 'Every third consecutive attack deals additional Magic Damage', on top of the 110s activation for resists. Both reward exactly the extended fight the page tells you to avoid without saying why.
audit.corrected: Relentless Assault ramps his attack speed the longer you stand there, and every third attack adds magic damage — short trades only.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and Leap Strike's range is never set against yours.
audit.why: Counter Strike 17s at rank 1, Leap Strike 8s at 700, Empower 7s down to 3s, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110s. Leap Strike reaches 700 against Shield Vault's 600 on 8s against your 13s — he closes further and more often, so you do not get to space him; you get to time Counter Strike's 17s.
audit.corrected: Numbers into the spikes, wants, early, mid, cooldown block and interactions row.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are entirely yours and you have to cash them — Jax is even-ish early and explodes at items, so every minute you waste is a minute closer to his takeover. Level 1 your point-and-click W stun plus an auto is one of the hardest level-1 commits in the game, and crucially he has NO Counter Strike yet to dodge it. Spike your level-2 W+Q all-in the instant you hit it, and at 3 run the full pattern: W-stun in, empowered-Q burst, E-block to ignore his return autos. The one rule: never dump your trade while his E is glowing — bait Counter Strike on the wave first, then commit.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are entirely yours and you have to cash them — Jax explodes at items, so every wasted minute is closer to his takeover. At 1 Shield Vault's 600-range leap-stun plus an auto is one of the hardest commits in the game, and he has NO Counter Strike yet. Spike the level-2 all-in immediately. Know what his E really does: it dodges ATTACKS, not abilities, so keep casting Q through it, stop auto-attacking, and never be mid-channel when it stuns. Bait its 17 seconds on the wave first, then run the full pattern: W-stun in, empowered-Q burst, and finish before Relentless Assault has ramped his attack speed on you.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are a knife's edge, so treat them as Skill, not free. You can still win short trades by E-blocking his Counter Strike window and resetting Q, but his Q-W gap-close plus the E stun now answers your all-in if you mistime it. At 6 your R is built for cross-map pressure, not for solo-killing a Jax who R's into huge defensive stats — so the correct play is to ULT OUT. Roam mid or bot with Grand Starfall, get a kill elsewhere, and turn this lane's tempo into a global lead before he ever sees an item.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are a knife's edge. Keep trades SHORT — Relentless Assault ramps his attack speed the longer you stand there, and every third attack under his ultimate adds magic damage. Leap Strike reaches 700 on 8s against your 600 on 13s, so you cannot space him; you time Counter Strike's 17s instead. At 6 Grandmaster-at-Arms hands him armour and magic resist, so the correct play is to ULT OUT: roam mid or bot with Grand Starfall, take a kill elsewhere, and turn this lane's tempo into a global lead before he ever finishes an item.

notes: The useful correction here is a narrowing rather than a fix: Riot's Counter Strike text says Jax 'dodges all incoming attacks', which is basic attacks, not abilities. Comet Spear and Shield Vault still land through the window, so the instruction changes from 'do not fight into E' to 'keep casting, stop auto-attacking, and never be mid-Aegis-Assault when the counterattack stuns' — that last part is the channel break _missing-interactions.json flags. Two mechanics were also entirely absent: Relentless Assault ramping his attack speed on consecutive attacks (the reason short trades beat long ones) and the passive half of Grandmaster-at-Arms adding magic damage every third attack.
